The Motor of the EVC

Technology & Innovation is the motor that drives the Electric Vehicle Center. U-M's faculty and labs partner with industry leaders to advance the technologies defining the next era of electrified mobility.

Our approach is collaborative by design. We start with the challenges our members need solved, then bring U-M's technical depth to bear. The result: a portfolio built with our partners, not just for them.

Our focus includes how to design, engineer, and manufacture better propulsion systems, batteries, and charging infrastructure. How they're used downstream is important work, but it's not our lane.

Eight Priority Technology Areas

8

Our research portfolio spans eight areas, prioritized by our industry members through structured roadmap workshops. These aren't arbitrary categories — they're what our industry partners told us matters most to their competitive future.

01 Batteries
02 Electric Machines & Drives
03 Thermal Management
04 Vehicle & Component End-of-Life
05 Electric Infrastructure & Charging Equipment
06 Data Collection, Modeling & Analysis
07 Raw Materials & Supply Chain
08 Lightweighting

Three Ways We Fund Great Research

3

Three project models, each meeting faculty and industry where they are.

01

Roadmap Projects

Multi-year, multi-PI

Multi-year, multi-PI programs launched in industry-driven waves. Round 1: batteries, electric drives, thermal management. Round 2: end-of-life and charging infrastructure. Round 3, in progress: lightweighting. Every project pairs U-M and industry co-PIs, with EVC funding U-M teams and companies contributing in-kind expertise, materials, and testing.

02

Direct Company-Faculty Projects

A meaningful nudge

When a company wants to work with a specific faculty member, the EVC contributes a 20% cost share. A small nudge, a meaningful difference.

03

Exploratory Seed Funding

Early-stage research

Early-stage research, including our MTRAC partnership and annual seed program.
